Rashi on Yevamot 16a:10:1.hebrew: עמון ומואב - ישראלים הדרים בארץ עמון ומואב שכיבש משה מסיחון ונתקדשו בקדושת א"י, ועכשיו בבית שני בטלה קדושתה וזורעין בשביעית. ותקנו להן מעשר ראשון ומעשר עני בשביעית, כדמפרש לקמן, מפני פרנסת עניים שבא"י שאין להם מה לאכול בשביעית, לפי שבטל לקט, שכחה ופיאה, והולכים שם ונוטלים לקט, שכחה ופיאה ומעשר עני:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:10:1.english: Ammon and Moab - [This refers to] Israelites dwelling in the land of Ammon and Moab, which Moses conquered from Sichon and [which] were sanctified with the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael, and now, in the [time of the] Second Temple, its sanctity was nullified, so they sow in the Sabbatical year. And [the Sages] instituted for them the first tithe and the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical year, as [the Gemara] explains below, for the sustenance of the poor in Eretz Yisrael who have nothing to eat in the Sabbatical year, since gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field are abolished [then], and they go there and take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, and the poor man's tithe.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:10:2.hebrew: ומקבלים גרים מן הקרדויין כו' - ולא אמרינן ממזרים הן מבנות ישראל שבאו עליהן עובדי כוכבים, דאיכא רבנן דפסלי:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:10:2.english: And one accepts converts from the Karduyin, etc. - And we do not say [that] they are mamzerim from Jewish women with whom idolaters cohabited, for there are Sages who disqualify [them].

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:11:1.english: He encountered him - Yonatan [encountered] Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:13:1.hebrew: וקדושה ראשונה - דבימי יהושע קדשה לשעתה ולא לעתיד. הלכך, זורעים בהן בשביעית, שיסמכו עליהן עניים לשכור עצמן לחרוש ולקצור, ועוד ליטול לקט, שכחה ופיאה ומעשר עני:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:13:1.english: And the initial consecration - [The consecration] in the days of Joshua sanctified [the land] for its time and not for the future. Therefore, they sow in them during the Sabbatical Year, so that the poor may rely upon them — to hire themselves out to plow and to harvest, and furthermore to take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner [of the field], and the poor man's tithe.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:15:1.english: One does not accept converts - [The Gemara] explains below that they are mamzerim [descended] from Israelites who assimilated there.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:17:1.english: The stains - That were found on garments coming from Rekem.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:17:2.english: [They are] ritually pure - Because [the Sages] did not decree [impurity] regarding the stains of idolaters.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:18:1.english: That they are converts - And their blood imparts ritual impurity.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:18:2.hebrew: וטועים - שהמירו דתם, וגזרו על כתמיהם, שאף על פי שחטאו שהמירו, ישראלים הם:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:18:2.english: And are in error - [Meaning] that they changed their religion, and [the Sages] decreed regarding their stains, for even though they sinned [in] that they apostatized, they are [still] Israelites.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:18:3.english: From among the idolaters - where no Jews live.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:1:1.hebrew: בני צרות - דב"ה דקא בעיתו אי הם פגומים:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:1:1.english: Children of rival wives - Of Beit Hillel, [concerning whom] you ask whether they are disqualified.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:1:2.english: I testify to you - that they are High Priests.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:2:1.hebrew: בימי ר' דוסא הותרה - אחיו של ר' דוסא, שהי' מתלמידי ב"ש, התירה, כדתני לקמן, ועשו על פיו ונהגו כן:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:2:1.english: In the time of Rabbi Dosa [she] was permitted - The brother of Rabbi Dosa, who was one of the students of Beit Shammai, permitted her, as [the Gemara] teaches below, and they acted according to his word and practiced thus.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:3:1.english: For he was a great Sage - And the Sages thought that he had permitted her.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:3:2.english: [His eyes] stood [still] - They stopped seeing.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:5:1.hebrew: אמר לו - רבי יהושע לר' דוסא, אמור לתלמידך אחר וישב:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:5:1.english: He said to him - Rabbi Yehoshua [said] to Rabbi Dosa: "Tell your other disciple to sit."

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:8:1.english: Dosa - Did you hear [people] saying [that] he permitted [it]?

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:8:3.hebrew: סתם שמענו - בן הרכינס סתם, ושמו לא הוזכר:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:8:3.english: We heard simply - [We heard] ben Harkinas unspecified, and his name was not mentioned.

Rashi on Yevamot 16a:8:4.hebrew: בכור שטן הוא - חריף, ועומד על שמועה, ועושה מעשה, ואינו שב משמועתו לעשות כרבים:
Rashi on Yevamot 16a:8:4.english: He is the firstborn of the Satan - [He is] sharp, and stands firm on [his] received teaching, and puts [it] into practice, and does not retract his teaching to act in accordance with the majority.

Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:11:1.hebrew: יצאו בג' פתחים - שלא ימצאם כולם יחד, ויקפחם בהלכות, ויצטרכו לקבוע הלכה כמותו. א"נ, יצאו בג' פתחים כדי שימצאו וישמעו תשובתו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:11:1.english: They left through three entrances - So that he would not find them all together and overwhelm them with halakhic [arguments], and they would have to establish the halakhah in accordance with his [view]. Alternatively, they left through three entrances so that they would find [him] and hear his response.

Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:13:1.hebrew: עמון ומואב מעשרין מעשר עני בשביעית - פי' בקונטרס: ישראלים הדרים בארץ עמון ומואב שכיבש משה מסיחון, ונתקדשו בקדושת הארץ, ועכשיו בבית שני בטלה קדושתה. וקשה לר"ת, דאמר בפ' מקום שנהגו (פסחים נב: ושם): "ג' ארצות לביעור: יהודה, ועבר הירדן, וגליל", ועבר הירדן היא ארץ סיחון ועוג — אלמא שקדשוה עולי בבל! ואומר ר"ת דהתם בארץ סיחון ועוג שלא היתה של עמון ומואב, אבל ארץ סיחון שכיבש מעמון ומואב לא קדשו עולי בבל, כדמשמע הכא. ועוד אמר ר"ת דמצינו למימר דהכא בארץ עמון ומואב שלא כיבש סיחון מעולם, שלא קדשוהו אפילו עולי מצרים; וכן משמע במס' ידים (פ"ד משנה ג), דמדמה לה מצרים ובבל. וה"פ הכא: דאמר מר "הרבה כרכים קדשו עולי מצרים ועולי בבל לא קדשו", והניחום כדי שיסמכו עליהם עניים — אלמא חששו לתקנת עניים; אע"ג דמא"י היו, נמנעו מלקדש. כל שכן בעמון ומואב שלא נתקדש מעולם, שראוי לתקן מעשר עני בשביעית, ולא מעשר שני — דבמס' ידים איכא מ"ד מעשר שני בשביעית. וכן יש לפרש במס' חגיגה (ד' ג. ושם), דקאמר נמי ר"א התם: "עמון ומואב מעשרין מעשר עני בשביעית", ומפרש: "מה טעם? הרבה כרכים כו'", ולא בעי למימר דעמון ומואב הוא מכרכים שכבשו עולי מצרים. ותדע, דהא לר"א מספקא ליה בפ"ק דמגילה (דף י.) ובפ"ב דשבועות (טז. ושם) אי סבר קדושה ראשונה קדשה לעתיד לבא או לא, ור' יהושע ס"ל דקדשה לעתיד לבא במגילה ובשבועות, ואפ"ה אית ליה במס' ידים בעמון ומואב כר"א! אלא על כרחך הא דקאמר התם "מה טעם" לא מדברי ר"א הוא, ודברי ר"א הם במס' ידים ולא קתני לה התם, אלא הש"ס הוא שמפר' כן: דלמ"ד לא קדשה, הניחו לקדש אף מא"י בשביל עניים, ולכך אין תימה אם גזרו על עמון ומואב מעשר עני ולא מעשר שני. והא דשבק הכא ובחגיגה טעמא דקאמר ר"ט בהדיא במסכת ידים: "מצרים ח"ל, עמון ומואב ח"ל; מה מצרים שהיא קרובה עשאוה מעשר עני כדי שיסמכו עליה עניים, אף עמון ומואב כו'" — משום דניחא ליה להש"ס דמשכחת טעמא דאף בא"י הניחו מלקדש בשביל עניים, וכ"ש עמון ומואב שהן ח"ל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:13:1.english: Ammon and Moab tithe the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical Year - Rashi explains: [This refers to] Israelites dwelling in the land of Ammon and Moab that Moses conquered from Sichon, which were sanctified with the sanctity of the Land [of Israel], and now in the Second Temple [era] its sanctity was nullified. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for it says in the chapter [entitled] Makom SheNahagu (Pesachim 52b and there): "[There are] three lands with respect to [the law of] removal: Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee," and Transjordan is the land of Sichon and Og — thus, those who ascended from Babylonia sanctified it! And Rabbeinu Tam says that there [in Pesachim it is speaking] of the land of Sichon and Og that did not belong to Ammon and Moab, whereas the land of Sichon that he conquered from Ammon and Moab was not sanctified by those who ascended from Babylonia, as is implied here. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam said that we can say that here [our Gemara is speaking] of the land of Ammon and Moab that Sichon never conquered, which even those who ascended from Egypt did not sanctify; and so it is implied in Tractate Yadayim (Chapter 4, Mishnah 3), which compares it to Egypt and Babylonia. And this is the explanation here: Since the Master said, "Many cities were sanctified by those who ascended from Egypt, and those who ascended from Babylonia did not sanctify [them]," and they left them [unsanctified] so that the poor might rely upon them — thus we see that they were concerned for the benefit of the poor; even though [those cities] were from the Land of Israel, they refrained from sanctifying [them]. All the more so in Ammon and Moab, which was never sanctified, it is fitting to institute the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical Year, and not the second tithe — for in Tractate Yadayim there is an opinion that says [they give] the second tithe in the Sabbatical Year. And so too should it be explained in Tractate Chagigah (3b and there), where Rabbi Eliezer also says there: "Ammon and Moab tithe the poor man's tithe in the Sabbatical Year," and it explains: "What is the reason? Many cities, etc." — and it does not mean to say that Ammon and Moab is among the cities that those who ascended from Egypt conquered. And know [that this is so], for Rabbi Eliezer is in doubt in the first chapter of Megillah (10a) and in the second chapter of Shevuot (16a and there) whether he holds that the initial consecration sanctified [the Land] for the future or not; and Rabbi Yehoshua holds in Megillah and in Shevuot that it sanctified [the Land] for the future, and even so, he holds like Rabbi Eliezer in Tractate Yadayim regarding Ammon and Moab! Rather, perforce, that which it says there [in Chagigah], "What is the reason?", is not from the words of Rabbi Eliezer — for the words of Rabbi Eliezer are in Tractate Yadayim and it does not teach this there — rather, it is the Gemara that explains it thus: that according to the one who says it did not sanctify [the Land for the future], they left even [cities] from the Land of Israel unsanctified for the sake of the poor, and therefore it is no wonder if they decreed the poor man's tithe, and not the second tithe, upon Ammon and Moab. And the reason it passed over here and in Chagigah the reason that Rabbi Tarfon states explicitly in Tractate Yadayim — "Egypt is outside the Land [of Israel], [and] Ammon and Moab are outside the Land [of Israel]; just as Egypt, which is nearby, was made [subject to] the poor man's tithe so that the poor might rely upon it, so too Ammon and Moab, etc." — is because the Gemara prefers to find a reason [showing] that even in the Land of Israel they refrained from sanctifying [cities] for the sake of the poor, and all the more so Ammon and Moab, which are outside the Land [of Israel].

Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:17:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן וסביא אמרי אין מקבלין גרים מן התרמודיים - תימה: היכי פליג ר' יוחנן אחגי הנביא? ושמא סבר ר' יוחנן שלא אמרה חגי מעולם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:17:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and the Elders say: One does not accept converts from the Tarmodim - It is astonishing: how does Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree with Haggai the prophet? Perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that Haggai never said it [i.e., that converts may be accepted from them].

Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:17:2.hebrew: כל הכתמים הבאים מרקם טהורים - אע"ג דברקם נמי הוו ישראל, כדתנן בריש גיטין (דף ב. ושם): "אף המביא מן הרקם ומן החגר", מ"מ כתמים הבאים מרקם טהורים, דלאו דישראלים נינהו; דישראל מצניעים כתמיהם, ועובדי כוכבים הדרים שם — עובדי כוכבים גמורים ולא ישראל מומרים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:17:2.english: All stains that come from Rekem are ritually pure - Even though in Rekem there were also Jews — as we learned in a Mishnah at the beginning of Gittin (2a and there [in the Gemara]): "Even one who brings [a bill of divorce] from Rekem and from Hagar" — nevertheless, stains that come from Rekem are ritually pure, because they do not belong to Jews, as Jews conceal their stains; and the gentiles who live there are full-fledged gentiles and not apostate Jews.

Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:1:1.hebrew: בני צרות אני מעיד לכם - דכשרים אף לב"ש. וא"ת: לשמואל דמספקא ליה בהאשה רבה (לקמן יבמות צב: ושם) אי קידושין תופסין ביבמ' לשוק, א"כ פשיטא דכשירה, דמיד שקדשה פקעה לה זיקה, כדאמרי' בשומרת יבם שקידש אחותה שקידושיה מפקיעין הייבום. וי"ל: דלא דמי, דהתם אין שום תקנה לעשות שתתייבם, שאין להמית אחותה; אבל היבמה שנתקדשה לשוק, אפשר לתקן ע"י גירושין שתתייבם, הלכך לא פקע זיקה. ועוד אמר רבי יצחק: ד"לא תהיה אשת המת לאיש זר" משמע דאפילו ע"י הויה, דהיינו קידושין, לא תהיה לאיש זר, דלהכי אפקיה בלשון הויה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 16a:1:1.english: Children of rival wives, I testify to you - [That is,] they are fit [to marry into the priesthood] even according to Beit Shammai. And if you ask: according to Shmuel, who is uncertain in [the chapter] HaIsha Rabbah (below, Yevamot 92b, and elsewhere), whether betrothal takes effect for a yevamah to an outsider — if so, it is obvious that she is fit, since as soon as he betrothed her, the levirate bond [zikah] is terminated, as we say regarding a woman awaiting a yavam whose sister he betrothed, that her betrothal terminates the levirate marriage! And one can answer: it is not comparable, for there, there is no remedy to enable her to enter into levirate marriage, since one cannot put her sister to death; however, regarding a yevamah who became betrothed to an outsider, it is possible to remedy [the situation] through divorce so that she can enter into levirate marriage, and therefore the levirate bond is not terminated. Furthermore, Rabbi Yitzchak said: [the verse] "the wife of the dead man shall not be [married] to a strange man" [Deuteronomy 25:5] implies that even through havayah [lit. "becoming"], which is betrothal, she shall not be [married] to a strange man, for that is why [Scripture] expressed it with the term havayah.
